newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fischer says A$ level at more accurate level.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fischer says A$ level at more accurate level.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister and Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Friday four cuts in official interest rates had helped create "a more accurate value of the Australian dollar which of course is helping exporters."
Fischer made the off-the-cuff remark at a business breakfast in Melbourne.

Later he told reporters: "Our good budget discipline...has helped facilitate four consecutive lowerings of interest rates and, as part of the flow-on from that, a slightly lower and more accurate value of the Australian dollar."
Fischer declined to say whether this remark meant the government was comfortable with the level of the local dollar against the greenback.
"A response to that particular question I would leave to my hard-working colleague (Treasurer) Peter Costello," he said.
Easier monetary policy has seen the Australian dollar shed about seven U.S. cents in value since it hit a high of US$0.82 late last year.
The Australian dollar was trading around US$0.7511/16 on Friday morning.
